title: The presheaf map from the etale sum presheaf to direct image is linear over the constant sheaf of rings
statement:
Let $\pi:U\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $\Lambda_X$ and $\Lambda_U$ the constant sheaves of rings with value $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites $X_{\Et}$ and $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $M$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_U$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an object $V$ of $X_{\Et}$ write $V_U=V\times_XU$ with projections $p_V:V_U\to V$, $q_V:V_U\to U$; for an $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$ write $(V,\varphi)$ for $V$ as an object of $U_{\Et}$ and $\Gamma_\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_V,\varphi):(V,\varphi)\to(V_U,q_V)$ for its graph, a morphism of $U_{\Et}$; let $e_\varphi:M(V,\varphi)\to M(V_U,q_V)$, the presheaf $P_M:V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,U)}M(V,\varphi)$ on $X_{\Et}$ and the morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ be those of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map] (with $P_M$ the presheaf of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=\pi$). Let $\gamma:\Lambda_X\to\pi_*\Lambda_U$ be the morphism of sheaves of rings of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1), induced through the universal property of sheafification by the constant sections, so that $\gamma_V:\Lambda_X(V)\to\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)$, and give the direct image $\pi_*M$, $(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V_U,q_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], its structure of sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules through $\gamma$: $f\cdot t=\gamma_V(f)\,t$ for $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$, $t\in M(V_U,q_V)$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3). For an $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$ let
$$\theta_{V,\varphi}=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi)\circ\gamma_V:\Lambda_X(V)\longrightarrow\Lambda_U(V,\varphi),$$
a ring homomorphism. Then:

1. For every morphism $a:V'\to V$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$, regarding $a$ as a morphism $(V',\varphi a)\to(V,\varphi)$ of $U_{\Et}$: $\theta_{V',\varphi a}(f|_{V'})=\Lambda_U(a)(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f))$ for all $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$.
2. Letting $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$ act on the summand $M(V,\varphi)$ of $P_M(V)$ by multiplication with $\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)$ makes $P_M$ a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (the restriction maps of $P_M$ are semilinear); this is the $\mathcal O$-module structure of Stacks, Modules on Sites, Lemma 03DI, $\theta_{V,\varphi}$ playing the role of the identification $\mathcal O_U(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)=\mathcal O(V)$. For a morphism $\alpha:M\to M'$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_U$-modules, $P_\alpha=\bigoplus_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}:P_M\to P_{M'}$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules.
3. For every $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$, $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$ and $s\in M(V,\varphi)$: $e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)\,s)=\gamma_V(f)\,e_\varphi(s)$. Consequently every $c^p_{M,V}:P_M(V)\to(\pi_*M)(V)$ is $\Lambda_X(V)$-linear for the structures of (2) and of $\pi_*M$ above, and $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules.

(Ingredients: $\gamma$ is a morphism of sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, so $\gamma_{V'}(f|_{V'})=\Lambda_U(a\times_X\mathrm{id}_U)(\gamma_V(f))$, and $(a\times_X\mathrm{id}_U)\circ\Gamma_{\varphi a}=\Gamma_\varphi\circ a$, which gives (1); (2) follows from (1) and the semilinearity of the restriction maps of $M$; for (3), $\gamma_V(f)e_\varphi(s)$ pulls back along $\Gamma_\varphi$ to $\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s$ and restricts to $0$ off $\Gamma_\varphi(V)$, so equals $e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s)$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](2).)

source.place: Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058) and its proof (the O-module structure f.s = fs on the presheaf V -> sum over phi of G(V -> U), with O_U(V/U)=O(V)); used in Etale Cohomology Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex line 11517), whose map is stated 'on abelian sheaves and sheaves of Lambda-modules' with the proof given only for abelian sheaves

proof.text: *Setting and the maps $\theta_{V,\varphi}$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](1), for an object $V$ of $X_{\Et}$ and an $X$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U$, $(V,\varphi)$ and $(V_U,q_V)$ are objects of $U_{\Et}$ and $\Gamma_\varphi:(V,\varphi)\to(V_U,q_V)$ is a morphism of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. $\Lambda_U$ is a sheaf of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so its restriction map $\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi):\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)\to\Lambda_U(V,\varphi)$ is a ring homomorphism; $\gamma:\Lambda_X\to\pi_*\Lambda_U$ is a morphism of sheaves of rings [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1), and $(\pi_*\Lambda_U)(V)=\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], so $\gamma_V:\Lambda_X(V)\to\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)$ is a ring homomorphism. Hence $\theta_{V,\varphi}=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi)\circ\gamma_V$ is a ring homomorphism. For a morphism $a:V'\to V$ of $X_{\Et}$ put $a_U=a\times_X\mathrm{id}_U:V'_U\to V_U$, the morphism with $p_Va_U=a\,p_{V'}$ and $q_Va_U=q_{V'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; it is a morphism $(V'_U,q_{V'})\to(V_U,q_V)$ of $U_{\Et}$, and the restriction map of a direct image $\pi_*F$ along $a$ is $F(a_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Also $a$ is a morphism $(V',\varphi a)\to(V,\varphi)$ of $U_{\Et}$, since $\varphi\circ a=\varphi a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof: the section s'_phi of F(V x_X U) pulling back to s_phi by Gamma_phi and restricting to zero off its image; the statement claims the map for sheaves of Lambda-modules, the proof treats abelian sheaves only

proof.text: *The graph identity.* For $a:V'\to V$ in $X_{\Et}$ and $\varphi:V\to U$ an $X$-morphism: $a_U\circ\Gamma_{\varphi a}=\Gamma_\varphi\circ a$ as morphisms $V'\to V_U$. Indeed $p_V a_U\Gamma_{\varphi a}=a\,p_{V'}\Gamma_{\varphi a}=a$ and $q_Va_U\Gamma_{\varphi a}=q_{V'}\Gamma_{\varphi a}=\varphi a$, while $p_V\Gamma_\varphi a=a$ and $q_V\Gamma_\varphi a=\varphi a$; two morphisms into $V_U=V\times_XU$ with the same two components are equal by the uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Lemma 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, line 11517), proof: the section s'_phi of F(V x_X U) pulling back to s_phi by Gamma_phi and restricting to zero off its image; the statement claims the map for sheaves of Lambda-modules, the proof treats abelian sheaves only

proof.text: *Clause 1.* Let $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$. Since $\gamma$ is a morphism of sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1) and the restriction of $\pi_*\Lambda_U$ along $a$ is $\Lambda_U(a_U)$ (step 1), $\gamma_{V'}(f|_{V'})=\Lambda_U(a_U)(\gamma_V(f))$. As $\Lambda_U$ is a contravariant functor on $U_{\Et}$, step 2 gives $\theta_{V',\varphi a}(f|_{V'})=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_{\varphi a})\Lambda_U(a_U)(\gamma_Vf)=\Lambda_U(a_U\Gamma_{\varphi a})(\gamma_Vf)=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi a)(\gamma_Vf)=\Lambda_U(a)\big(\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi)(\gamma_Vf)\big)=\Lambda_U(a)(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f))$.

source.place: Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058), proof, first paragraph: f.s = fs with O_U(V -> U) = O(V)

proof.text: *Clause 2: $P_M$ is a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules.* $M(V,\varphi)$ is a $\Lambda_U(V,\varphi)$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], hence a $\Lambda_X(V)$-module through the ring homomorphism $\theta_{V,\varphi}$ (step 1); so $P_M(V)=\bigoplus_\varphi M(V,\varphi)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is a $\Lambda_X(V)$-module, $f\cdot(s_\varphi)_\varphi=(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s_\varphi)_\varphi$, whose additive group is that of the presheaf of abelian groups $P_M$. This is the structure $f\cdot s=fs$ of Stacks 03DI, with $\theta_{V,\varphi}$ in place of $\mathcal O_U(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)=\mathcal O(V)$. Semilinearity: for $a:V'\to V$, the restriction $P_M(a)$ sends $s\in M(V,\varphi)$ to $M(a)(s)$ in the summand of $\varphi a$ (with $a:(V',\varphi a)\to(V,\varphi)$, step 1). By the semilinearity of the restriction maps of the $\Lambda_U$-module $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and clause 1 (step 3), $M(a)(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s)=\Lambda_U(a)(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f))\,M(a)(s)=\theta_{V',\varphi a}(f|_{V'})\,M(a)(s)=f|_{V'}\cdot M(a)(s)$. Since $P_M(a)$ is additive and every element of $P_M(V)$ is a finite sum of elements of the summands, $P_M(a)(f\cdot s)=f|_{V'}\cdot P_M(a)(s)$ for all $s\in P_M(V)$ (several $\varphi$ with the same $\varphi a=\psi$ land in the summand of $\psi$, where they are added, and the action of $f|_{V'}$ there is additive). As $\Lambda_X$ is a sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $P_M$ is a presheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $\alpha:M\to M'$, each $\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$ is $\Lambda_U(V,\varphi)$-linear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], hence $\Lambda_X(V)$-linear through $\theta_{V,\varphi}$, so $(P_\alpha)_V=\bigoplus_\varphi\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$ is $\Lambda_X(V)$-linear; and $(P_\alpha)_{V'}\circ P_M(a)=P_{M'}(a)\circ(P_\alpha)_V$ because on the summand of $\varphi$ both sides are $\alpha_{(V',\varphi a)}\circ M(a)=M'(a)\circ\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$ into the summand of $\varphi a$ ($\alpha$ is a morphism of presheaves). So $P_\alpha$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Lemma 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero, line 2058), proof, first paragraph: f.s = fs with O_U(V -> U) = O(V)

proof.text: *Clause 3: the identity $e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s)=\gamma_V(f)e_\varphi(s)$.* Let $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$, $s\in M(V,\varphi)$, and $t=\gamma_V(f)\,e_\varphi(s)\in M(V_U,q_V)$, the product for the $\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)$-module $M(V_U,q_V)$. Let $W=V_U\setminus\Gamma_\varphi(V)$, open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](1), with inclusion $j_W$, a morphism $(W,q_Vj_W)\to(V_U,q_V)$ of $U_{\Et}$; restriction of sections to $W$ is $M(j_W)$. By semilinearity of the restriction maps of $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](2) ($M(\Gamma_\varphi)(e_\varphi s)=s$, $M(j_W)(e_\varphi s)=0$): $M(\Gamma_\varphi)(t)=\Lambda_U(\Gamma_\varphi)(\gamma_Vf)\,M(\Gamma_\varphi)(e_\varphi s)=\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)\,s$ and $M(j_W)(t)=\Lambda_U(j_W)(\gamma_Vf)\,M(j_W)(e_\varphi s)=\Lambda_U(j_W)(\gamma_Vf)\cdot0=0$. So $t$ satisfies the two conditions characterizing $e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s)$, and by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](2), $t=e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s)$. (This uses only semilinearity, not that $f$ is a constant section: $\Lambda_X(V)$ consists of locally constant functions, not only constants.)

proof.text: *Clause 3: linearity of $c^p_M$.* $\pi_*M$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules with $f\cdot u=\gamma_V(f)u$ for $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$, $u\in(\pi_*M)(V)=M(V_U,q_V)$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3), [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $s=(s_\varphi)_\varphi\in P_M(V)$ (finitely many nonzero components) and $f\in\Lambda_X(V)$, by step 4 and step 5, $c^p_{M,V}(f\cdot s)=\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(\theta_{V,\varphi}(f)s_\varphi)=\sum_\varphi\gamma_V(f)e_\varphi(s_\varphi)=\gamma_V(f)\sum_\varphi e_\varphi(s_\varphi)=f\cdot c^p_{M,V}(s)$, using the distributivity of the $\Lambda_U(V_U,q_V)$-module $M(V_U,q_V)$. $c^p_{M,V}$ is additive and $c^p_M$ commutes with the restriction maps, since it is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-etale-graph-section-extension-map](3). A morphism of presheaves of abelian groups between presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules that is $\Lambda_X(V)$-linear on every $V$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; with step 4 ($P_M$ is one), $c^p_M:P_M\to\pi_*M$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules.

Statement and stmt_deps kept. The brief's plan (pull f through e_phi as a constant section) does not cover non-constant f in Lambda_X(V) (locally constant functions); the uniqueness argument of the statement's own ingredients is used instead. proof_origin is agent: Stacks 0F4L claims the map for Lambda-modules but proves only the abelian case; 03DI gives the module structure.
